gloss: bald at the front, bare front area
summary: Leviticus distinguishes hair loss at the front of the scalp from the reddish-white mark a priest examines there. Later in the chapter the same noun describes part of a textile or leather article.

senses.gloss: bald at the front of the head
senses.definition: Describes a person whose hair has receded from the face.

evidence.note: The law describes hair loss on the side toward the face and declares the person clean.

words.gloss: bare front of the scalp or of material

senses.gloss: bald area at the front of the head
senses.definition: The exposed skin at the front of a balding scalp.

evidence.note: A reddish-white mark may appear on either of the two bald areas distinguished in the preceding verses.
The priest looks at the swelling on the bald patch and examines its colour.

senses.gloss: bare area on the front or face of material
senses.definition: One of two contrasted areas where damage can remain visible on a washed article of cloth or leather.

evidence.note: The priest inspects the washed article. The paired terms previously used of the scalp now locate the damage on the material.

evidence.locator: s.v. ܓܒܚܘܬܐ, baldness on the forepart of the head

note: The Syriac noun specifies the same part of the scalp. The Akkadian adjective describes baldness more generally, and its historical connection is uncertain. Leviticus 13:55 transfers the scalp terminology to material. Which aspect of the material’s surface the pair distinguishes remains open.
